title: Adaptive tier allocator and soft-fallback sequencing for quota-aware routing
creator: Rohit Singh
description: Problem: Customers in different plan tiers (free, paid, enterprise) share our serving surface. Under bursty load and regional capacity constraints we need a deterministic, quota-aware allocator that preserves enterprise SLOs, gives paid customers fair throughput, and provides graceful, measurable fallback behavior for free-tier requests. Current behavior is ad-hoc: some free traffic gets silently dropped or causes head-of-line blocking for higher tiers. This ticket designs and implements an adaptive allocator and soft-fallback sequencing to make behavior predictable, observable, and reversible.
proposed_solution: Introduce a Tier Allocator component in the front-line admission controller that: 1) maintains per-tenant and per-tier sliding quota windows (minute and hour buckets) to compute available allowance; 2) assigns requests to priority lanes with admission scores computed from tier weight, remaining allowance, and latency SLO headroom; 3) implements soft-fallback sequencing where when a request is denied full-tier dispatch it is retried against a cheaper model variant or routed to reduced-cost execution paths (smaller context / lower temperature / response truncation) rather than being dropped; 4) supports regional spillover: if region capacity is constrained, low-priority lanes are routed to alternative regions or queued up to a short max-delay; 5) exposes signals for realtime decisions and downstream telemetry (reason codes, matched-tier, fallback-path, original-request-id). The component is feature-flagged and configurable per-customer via Console.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic admission: given synthetic workloads we can reproduce lane assignment decisions using a recorded seed and configuration
Enterprise SLOs preserved: enterprise 95th latency regression < 5% vs baseline under the same load when allocator is enabled
Fairness: paid plan median throughput improves vs current baseline under mixed workload (metric: tokens/sec per paid-customer 95th percentile)
Soft-fallback correctness: at least 95% of denied full-tier dispatches complete successfully via fallback path and return structured reason codes
Observability: Console shows per-tier allowance, fallback rate, longest-queue, and a new "fallback_reason" dimension in traces
Feature-flag rollout: can disable allocator globally and per-region without restarting serving hosts
rollout_plan: Start behind a kill-switch. Phase A: unit/integration tests and internal canary with 5% of traffic (non-customer simulated workspace) for 72 hours. Phase B: 0.5% of production customers (non-enterprise) for 24 hours, monitor errors and fallback rate. Phase C: increase to 10% including paid customers, validate cost deltas and latency SLOs. Phase D: enable defaults for all free/paid customers while enterprise customers are pinned to reserved lanes. Each phase has explicit rollback thresholds (error rate +3% absolute, fallback_rate > 25%, P95 latency regression > 7%).
risks: Mis-calibrated allowance can starve paid customers if weights are wrong
Fallback models might produce lower quality responses impacting user experience
Telemetry tagging gaps could make incidents hard to diagnose
Cross-region spillover could increase end-to-end latency for low-tier customers
Edge cases where multi-request flows (chat sessions) lose context when falling back to trimmed variants
tasks: Design: finalize scoring function and allowance window sizes (SRE + Research)
API: extend admission controller API to accept tier and allowance metadata
Runtime: implement Tier Allocator module and integrate with dispatcher
Fallback: add model-variant registry and fallback sequencing engine
Observability: add metrics, traces, and Console widgets
E2E tests: synthetic mixed-workload harness and chaos tests for region failures
Docs: Console docs for per-customer knob and runbook for incidents
Rollout: implement feature-flag gating and canary automation
